Question B-003-018-002.

Why the correct answer is right: Removing the microphone takes away the usual transmit control, reducing the chance of unauthorized mobile use.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Remove the microphone when you are not using it": This is the correct choice because removing the microphone takes away the usual transmit control, reducing the chance of unauthorized mobile use.
- sourceIndex 1: "Tune the radio to an unused frequency when you are done using it": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Remove the microphone when you are not using it. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "Turn the radio off when you are not using it": This answer would fit a different fault than Remove the microphone when you are not using it. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Put a \"Do not touch\" sign on the radio": This option confuses another station topic with Remove the microphone when you are not using it. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, a warning sign or room arrangement is not a positive control for the hazard in this item.
